chunks: From him, from some of his companions, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the skins of wild beasts, so he said: 'Ride on them, and do not wear anything from them in which you pray.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing wild animal skins during Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the permissibility of using wild animal skins for riding (*rukub*) and their imperability for wearing during prayer (*salat*). This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that while these skins are not inherently impure (*najis*) to the point of prohibiting use, they lack the ritual purity required for the specific act of worship, highlighting the distinction between general utility and ritual validity in fiqh.
